renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: evidence_dot_plot
  title: Fusion evidence by splice pattern
  description: |-
    Each dot is a fusion call placed under its splice pattern, coloured by its abundance (log10 of FFPM plus one) and sized by the share of its evidence that crosses the junction itself. It answers which fusions have the strongest and most direct support.
    How to read: large, dark dots are abundant fusions backed mostly by junction reads, the most convincing kind. Small, pale dots rest on spanning fragments alone and deserve a second look.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: splice_type
    gene: fusion
    mean_expression: log_ffpm
    frac_expressing: junction_fraction

- component: figure
  title: Supporting reads per fusion
  description: |-
    Each bar is a fusion call: the sum of its junction reads and spanning fragments, coloured by splice pattern. It answers which fusions have the most evidence.
    How to read: tall bars are well supported. STAR-Fusion's defaults keep only calls with at least two supporting fragments, so the shortest bars are near the filter.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/STAR-Fusion/STAR-Fusion/master/STAR-Fusion
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: fusion
    y: supporting_reads
    color: splice_type
    labels:
      fusion: Fusion
      supporting_reads: Supporting reads (junction reads plus spanning fragments)
      splice_type: Splice pattern

- component: card
  title: Fusion abundance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median abundance of the calls on a log10 scale of fusion fragments per million (plus one), and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how strongly fusions are expressed.
    How to read: higher values mean more fusion fragments per million RNA-seq fragments. STAR-Fusion's defaults keep only calls with at least 0.1 FFPM, so every call here passed that floor.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/STAR-Fusion/STAR-Fusion/master/STAR-Fusion
  column: log_ffpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: log10 FFPM plus one, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Fusions called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct fusions called, and the bars rank the splice patterns that account for most of them. It answers how many fusion candidates there are and how they splice.
    How to read: review the less common patterns against the evidence plot before reporting them.
  column: fusion
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: splice_type
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: fusions, by splice pattern
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Supporting reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of junction reads and spanning fragments over all calls, and the ring splits it by splice pattern. It answers where the evidence comes from.
    How to read: a ring dominated by one pattern means most evidence sits on that kind of splice.
  column: supporting_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: splice_type
  caption: reads, by splice pattern

- component: card
  title: Junction evidence share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean share of each call's evidence that crosses the junction itself rather than spanning it, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how direct the evidence is.
    How to read: values near one mean the call is backed by reads over the breakpoint. Calls near zero rest on spanning fragments only.
  column: junction_fraction
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share of evidence at the junction

- component: table
  title: STAR-Fusion calls
  description: |-
    Each row is a fusion call with its partner genes, breakpoints, splice pattern, read evidence, FFPM and annotations. It answers which fusions to validate.
    How to read: sort by supporting reads or FFPM and check the annotations for known cancer fusions.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: fusion
